stories.notes: Boundary-condition bug fix (off-by-one at age 65). AC are already specific and well-scoped — fix, regression guard (age 64), and non-regression of other behaviors are all stated, so openspec elaboration is not needed. Assigning speckit only to harden testability and flag edge-case gaps, e.g. a rider aged exactly 65 who also holds a pass (AC only covers no-pass scenarios), and to verify the boundary is inclusive (>=65) across all fare-rule code paths.

agentContributions.notes: Defect: fareFor uses strict > (now >= in code shown but the bug was >) at the senior boundary, so age 65 falls through to BASE_FARE_CENTS. Fix site is the comparison in fareFor. VCs are black-box checks on the fare value returned for each boundary case.

Read src/fares.ts and test/fares.test.ts to ground the review. The code has three fare paths: hasPass→0, age≥65→concession, age<13→concession, else base. The original AC 'The existing fare behaviour for children, pass holders and adults is unchanged' was too vague — it bundled three distinct categories into one untestable blanket statement. I decomposed it into four specific observable sub-cases (ACs 4–7) that each assert a concrete fare value for a concrete rider. I also added AC 3 (age 66) to confirm the senior boundary works above the fix point, and ACs 7–8 to cover the pass-priority interaction at both boundary ages (65 and 12), since the hasPass check short-circuits before the age checks and a regression could silently break that priority. No splitting proposed — that is openspec's decision alone.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both manifest paths exist and are verified exact against the repository. All five verification criteria are concrete, black-box, and observable — each asserts a specific fare value (175, 350, or 0) for a specific rider input (age + hasPass). They correctly cover the boundary (age 65 → 175, age 64 → 350), non-regression (child age 8 → 175, pass-holder age 30 → 0, adult age 30 → 350), and the pass-priority short-circuit. Both agents contributed non-overlapping value: openspec identified the defect mechanism (strict > at the senior boundary) and confirmed VCs are black-box fare-value checks; speckit grounded its review in the actual source, decomposed the vague 'existing behaviour unchanged' AC into specific observable sub-cases, and flagged edge-case gaps (age 66, pass-priority at boundary ages). The guardVocabulary is well-constructed — it blacklists implementation-mechanism terms (constant names, operators, branching, docstring) and whitelists observable surface terms (fareFor, returns, fare values in cents). HOWEVER: the fixSiteAnalysis for src/fares.ts sets changeRequired=true and prescribes changing `rider.age > 65` to `rider.age >= 65`, but the actual source code (line 10) already reads `rider.age >= 65`. The described bug is already fixed in the repository. openspec's own notes acknowledge this ('now >= in code shown but the bug was >'). An implementer following this spec would find nothing to change in src/fares.ts. The VCs all pass against the current code, so the spec remains implementable (trivially), making this advisory rather than blocking. The test file already asserts the correct boundary values (age 65 → CONCESSION_FARE_CENTS, age 64 → BASE_FARE_CENTS) and needs no edit, consistent with the fixSiteAnalysis deliveryRole=verifies, changeRequired=false for that file.
